## Project 1: StallSeeker – Real-Time Android Food Stall Discovery Application {.unnumbered}

### My Responsibilities {.unnumbered}
- Developed the Android application frontend using Flutter and Dart for nearby food stall discovery, search, filters, and self-collect bookings.
- Implemented customer and vendor features using Firebase Authentication, Firestore, and Storage for account access, menus, and stock management.
- Integrated Google Maps and GPS for live vendor tracking/navigation and Stripe sandbox payments.
- Created automated Android UI testing scripts using Appium, Python, and pytest with HTML reporting.

### Technologies Used {.unnumbered}
- Flutter & Dart
- Firebase (Authentication, Cloud Firestore, Firebase Storage, Cloud Messaging, Cloud Functions)
- Google Maps API & GPS
- Stripe Sandbox API
- Appium, Python, pytest

### Challenges experienced {.unnumbered}
- Making the UI fit well on different screen sizes like web browsers, tablets, and phones without layout issues.
- Fixing a navigation bug where going back to a previous page refreshed the whole screen and cleared the user's progress.

### Solutions {.unnumbered}
- Adjusted the layout sizes and tested the app manually on different screen sizes and emulators.
- Updated the page navigation and saved the page state so going back keeps the user's data without reloading everything.


## Project 2: Expense Tracker {.unnumbered}

### My Responsibilities {.unnumbered}
- Built the frontend user interface in Next.js for recording expenses, categorizing transactions, and viewing spending summaries.
- Developed the backend REST API using NestJS to handle authentication, expense CRUD operations, and category filtering.
- Connected the backend to a PostgreSQL database using Prisma ORM and designed the relational schema for users and expense records.

### Technologies Used {.unnumbered}
- Next.js (React)
- NestJS
- TypeScript
- Prisma ORM
- PostgreSQL
- Git

### Challenges experienced {.unnumbered}
- Coordinating the full-stack data flow between the Next.js frontend forms, NestJS API routes, Prisma ORM queries, and PostgreSQL tables, particularly handling authentication headers and keeping frontend/backend data types aligned.

### Solutions {.unnumbered}
- Defined structured REST endpoints with DTO validation in NestJS and configured Prisma schema migrations so database models stayed consistent with the JSON payloads sent from the Next.js frontend.
